reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that TiC can be uniformly dispersed in a W matrix and improves high-temperature and irradiation properties, supporting the feasibility of dispersion and general high-temperature benefit. However, it does not address W–Cu composites, Cu matrices, or the specific mechanisms of inhibiting phase separation and interfacial void formation between W and Cu, leaving key premises unsupported.
premises: TiC can be uniformly dispersed in a W-based composite, both within grains and along grain boundaries.
TiC dispersion improves high-temperature stability and irradiation resistance of W-based materials.
TiC at interfaces/grain boundaries can act as a stabilizer to inhibit phase separation and void formation in a W–Cu composite.
